name: Tile-Based Volume Rendering
definition: A rendering technique that splits the image plane into tiles of closely related pixels to limit data access and improve cache locality. Voxels and data accessed during the tracing of one ray are reused for other rays close to the first one. All frame estimates for a tile are computed one after another to prevent cache replacement.
summary: Tile-Based Volume Rendering splits the image plane into tiles to improve cache locality and limit data access, distinguishing itself from Marching Caches by relying on spatial locality within fixed tiles rather than an explicit shared cache.
